# Paper podcast — Style Prompt

> A warm podcast-style talking head where the story is told across a table of paper. The speaker's face stays on screen as shot and carries the film; beside it, above it or on the chest, the line's world turns into objects you could hold: a recipe card, a ledger sheet, a telegram, a instant photo, a sticky note, each landing on its word and getting written, stamped or circled as it is said. Captions are one or two words on a navy card under the chin, a small line over one big word or a handwritten key word. Film grain and dust over everything, a slow 4 % drift, at most three punch-ins, one full-screen card of at most 2.5 s.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

1. **The face is the stage.** The speaker is on screen at least 65 % of the film, as shot: no grade, no filter, no vignette on the face. Paper sits beside (left or right column), above (top band) or below (chest band) the face, never on it, also under a punch-in.
2. **Every idea becomes a tactile object** from the story's world (what would a person in that story physically hold at that moment?), and the spoken claim appears on it as it is said: written by hand, printed, stamped, circled.
3. **Two-tier captions**: a small line, then one big bold word, or a key word in handwriting, on a navy card under the chin. One text layer at a time: a chest prop that carries the words hides the caption.
4. **Warmth lives in the paper**, never in a grade: navy and kraft surfaces, cream paper, blue pen, a red marker.
5. **Restraint in the camera**: a slow drift all the way, at most three comic punch-ins, a full-screen card only for the one proof moment (≤ 2.5 s).

Not a paper collage film (the face is never replaced for long). Not a subtitle track (never a full sentence on screen, never word-by-word karaoke). Not a sepia or vintage filter on the person. Not stickers flying over the face.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Footage**: the user's talking-head clip from `list_media` as one `<video>` (`assets/media/upl_<id>.mp4`) inside `#zoom` (`object-fit: cover`), shot vertical, face in the upper middle. Reframe a horizontal clip to vertical (craft `reframe.md`), never pillar-box it. Read the face position from the contact sheet of `inspect_media` and place the columns in the free space (in the example the head spans x 330-750, chin ≈ y 1100). The example paints a stand-in (a warm room with lamp bokeh and a person drawn as SVG, alive with a head bob, blinks and a moving mouth on the speech windows); replace `#ruang` and `#plate` with the video.
- **Captions and words from speech**: take `words {text,start,end}` from `inspect_media`'s transcript (or the user's script) and put each caption on its word: start = first word's `start`, swap on the next caption's start. Check names and prices with the user.
- **Cutouts** are not needed here: nothing goes behind the person. If a prop must overlap the shoulder line, keep it on the chest band below the chin.
- **Paper**: cream sheets (`--kertas`) with a 6 px radius and a soft contact shadow (0 22 50 at 50 %), ruled lines every 64 px in a pale blue (`--garis`), a strip of masking tape (`--lakban` at 88 %) on top, typewriter lines on a telegram strip (`--kertas-2`) with each word in its own cream box, a sticky note (`--stiker`), instant photos (cream frame, 18 px border, deep label strip).
- **Full-screen card**: `--latar` with a radial lift of `--latar-2` at 50 % 40 %, a vignette to 40 % at the edges, the content pushed in 1.00 → 1.05 linearly.
- **Texture**: one film-grain image (seeded noise, overlay at 9 %) and one dust image (specks and hairs, 50 %), each painted once and offset every frame by the frame number (seek-safe, never by wall-clock time). Over everything, including the face (texture only, no colour change).
- Inline SVG for drawn objects (a jar, a ticket, a map) when the user has no photo; the user's own photo from `list_media` goes in the instant photo first.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar` is the navy of the caption card (at 86 %) and the full-screen card; `--latar-2` its radial lift. `--teks` is the caption ink; the handwritten key word on the card uses `--aksen-di-latar` (a warm cream-gold).
- `--utama` fills the rubber stamp (with `--teks-di-utama` lettering): the one brand stroke on the paper.
- Fixed in every brand, because paper is paper: `--kertas`, `--kertas-2`, `--garis`, `--lakban`, `--stiker`, `--kraft`, the ink `--tinta`, the blue pen `--pena`, and the red `--merah` for marker circles and red figures on a ledger. A pale brand turns the caption card white with dark words; that is correct.
- The stand-in footage colours (`--f-*`) never change; the user's video is never recoloured.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` carries the big caption word at 800, 132 px, tracking −4 px, line-height 0.98 (16:9: 100 px), the plain one-line caption at 80 px / −2 px (16:9: 62 px) and big figures on paper (78 px). Inter 800 in the example; a tight grotesque (Archivo Black, Poppins 800) also suits. Size the big word to fit 960 px: long words drop to 0.62 of their width budget.
- `--font-isi` carries the small caption line at 600, 62 px, tracking −1.5 px (16:9: 46 px), and printed headings on paper (22-30 px caps, 800).
- Look faces (fixed): Caveat 700 for handwriting and the key-word caption (150 px on the card, 40-76 px on paper), IBM Plex Mono 600 caps for typed lines (48 px, tracking 1 px), Oswald 700 caps for the stamp (76 px, tracking 3 px).
- One or two words per caption, lowercase except names; a full sentence never.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Caption in**: 0.12 s `power2.out`, from y +12 px and scale 0.96, opacity 0 → 1; **out**: a hard swap on the next caption's word. Captions change every 1.2-2 s.
- **Prop entrances** (pick per object, never the same twice in a row): slap (scale 1.28 → 1 with 4° of turn, 0.14 s `power4.in`), drop (from y −420 and −14° to its tilt, 0.5 s `back.out(1.4)`), rise (from y +520, 0.42 s `back.out(1.3)`), side (from x ±260 and 9°, 0.42 s `back.out(1.3)`), swing (from 34° about its tape, 1.1 s `elastic.out(1, 0.35)`), toss (from far right with 18°, 0.46 s `power3.out`). Props rest tilted −5° to +5°.
- **Prop exits**: 0.2 s fade; a chest prop drops away (y +700, 0.32 s `power2.in`).
- **Marks on the word**: handwriting wipes in left → right by `clip-path` in 0.5-0.8 s `power1.out`; a marker ellipse draws by `stroke-dashoffset` 1 → 0 in 0.4 s `power1.inOut`; a stamp slams from scale 2.3 and −8° in 0.18 s `power4.in`; typed lines appear in three steps (`steps(3)`) over 0.5 s; a figure lands from scale 1.7 at 25 % opacity in 0.25 s and counts up over 0.6 s `power3.out`.
- **Full-screen card**: in by iris (circle 0 → 75 % at 50 % 45 %, 0.3 s `power2.in`), push or wipe; out by wipe (0.22 s `power2.inOut`); ≤ 2.5 s on screen.
- **Holds**: a prop stays 2-3.5 s; the ending holds ≥ 2 s with the caption and the last prop still.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Slow drift 1.00 → 1.04 over the whole film, linear | the conversation is alive | always, under everything |
| Punch-in 1.0 → 1.1 in 0.12 s `power3.out`, back in 0.22 s after ~0.8 s, pivoting on the mouth line | the punchline, the surprising number | at most three per film |
| Iris into a full-screen card | stepping into the memory or the proof | one proof moment, ≤ 2.5 s |
| Wipe out of the card | back to the speaker | after the card |
| Hard cut between takes | the default; jump cuts are hidden by the caption swap | everything else |

## 7. Native moves

- **The object finishes the line.** On frame 1 a paper object from the first line's world is already beside the face (slapped in), and the pen writes its title while the caption says the first words. *Fits content like:* a grandmother's recipe card for a home bakery; a boarding pass for a travel creator; a timetable for a teacher's first lesson; the first page of a diary in a short story.
- **Ledger number.** A ruled sheet drops into a side column, the figure lands big in red and counts up while the caption shows a small line over the same number; one punch-in on it. *Fits content like:* "1.240 toples terjual"; a channel's subscriber count; a class's pass rate; the years a character waited.
- **Instant photo proof.** One full-screen navy card opens by iris, a instant photo is tossed in with a handwritten label, a stamp slams on its corner, the card wipes away within 2.5 s. *Fits content like:* the first jar sold; a before photo of a shop; the first video a creator posted; a family photo in a memoir.
- **Telegram on the chest.** A typed strip rises below the chin, its lines appear on their words in stepped typing, a marker circles the one word that matters; the caption steps aside. *Fits content like:* "rahasianya bukan resepnya, tapi catatannya"; a rule of a class; a supplier's message; a letter that turns a story.
- **Handwritten key word.** The caption card carries one word in handwriting in the accent instead of the bold word. *Fits content like:* the podcast's name; a feeling ("rindu"); the product's nickname; the lesson's single idea.
- **Sticky-note sign-off.** A sticky note swings in on its tape with the episode, the schedule and a contact, beside the face, held to the end. *Fits content like:* "Eps. 12 · tiap Jumat"; opening hours and chat; the next class date; "bersambung".

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Paper on the face**: measure the face box over the whole film (bob, drift and punch-ins included); a column prop that touches it moves out or shrinks. Captions never reach the chin.
- **Two text layers at once**: a chest prop that carries words hides the caption for its duration.
- **Grading the person**: never warm, sepia or vignette the speaker; warmth comes from paper.
- **Too many punch-ins**: more than three (or one on every cut) reads as annoying.
- **Full-screen card too long**: over 2.5 s the face is lost; keep one, for the proof.
- **Captions that hide too late**: hide each caption with an explicit tween after its entrance, not a bare set inside the fade.
- **Wall-clock texture**: grain and dust offsets come from the frame number, or renders will not match previews.
- **Performance**: move the grain and dust images by transform only; the stand-in plate redraws a handful of SVG attributes per frame; no blur on large layers.

## Measured from the references

From the source's Face RESULT builder: small caption line 62 px, big word 132 px, key word 150 px in handwriting, card at 86 % navy with a 26 px radius and 12/36/18 px padding; face on screen ≥ 65 %; full-screen cards ≤ 2.5 s; ≤ 3 punch-ins; drift 4 %; held tail 0.45 s; props kept inside the safe area (top 220, bottom 1500 at 1080 × 1920).

# Paper podcast: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2.0, medium 3.0, long 3.6.

## hook

- en: face from frame 1, a paper object already slapped beside it, the line in a two-tier navy caption, handwriting writes its title
- id: wajah sejak frame 1, benda kertas sudah menempel di sampingnya, caption dua tingkat di kartu navy, tulisan tangan menulis judulnya

## problem

- en: a crumpled note or bill drops into a side column on the trouble word; the bad word big in the caption; one punch-in
- id: catatan atau tagihan jatuh ke kolom samping pada kata masalahnya; kata buruknya besar di caption; satu punch-in

## fact

- en: a telegram strip rises onto the chest, its lines typed on the words, a marker circles the key word; caption hidden
- id: telegram naik ke dada, barisnya diketik pada katanya, spidol melingkari kata kuncinya; caption disembunyikan

## step

- en: index cards land one per step in the side column, each numbered by hand on its word; the step word big in the caption
- id: kartu indeks mendarat satu per langkah di kolom samping, nomornya ditulis tangan pada katanya; kata langkah besar di caption

## compare

- en: two instant photos, one per side column, before and after, labelled by hand; the face stays between them
- id: dua instant photo di kolom kiri dan kanan, sebelum dan sesudah, berlabel tulisan tangan; wajah tetap di antaranya

## number

- en: a ledger sheet drops beside the face, the figure slams in big in red and counts up; small line + big number caption, punch-in
- id: lembar catatan jatuh di samping wajah, angkanya menghentak besar merah lalu menghitung; caption baris kecil + angka besar, punch-in

## proof

- en: one full-screen navy card (≤ 2.5 s) opens by iris, a instant photo of the proof is tossed in, a stamp slams on it
- id: satu kartu navy layar penuh (≤ 2,5 dtk) dibuka iris, instant photo buktinya dilempar masuk, cap dihentak di atasnya

## offer

- en: a price tag or receipt slaps beside the face, the price circled in marker; the item name big in the caption
- id: label harga atau struk menempel di samping wajah, harganya dilingkari spidol; nama barangnya besar di caption

## cta

- en: the name in Caveat handwriting on the navy caption, a sticky note with the time and contact swings in; held 2.5 s
- id: nama ditulis tangan di kartu caption navy, catatan tempel berisi jadwal dan kontak berayun masuk; diam 2,5 dtk

## payoff

- en: the hook's paper object comes back beside the face with one new handwritten word; Caveat key word caption, held 2 s
- id: benda kertas pembuka kembali di samping wajah dengan satu kata baru tulisan tangan; caption kata kunci Caveat, diam 2 dtk
